root_cause: The ledger reserved spend before dispatch but client errors lost transport-phase evidence; the worker continued the claimed batch during adapter outage.

implementation.classification: UNSENT_CALL_REASONS in semantic_extraction_client.py is the single exhaustive allowlist. DNS/refused socket errors qualify only inside connect(); adapter policy refusal requires the top-level structured error_code, never substring matching. Direct pre-invoke policy, absent transport, admission and input-budget refusals are explicitly tracked too. Sent/ambiguous errors, streaming timeout, provider errors, billing errors and process crashes remain spent.
implementation.ledger: Reserve atomically before call (cap and per-source limits remain enforced); proven unsent outcomes atomically decrement original UTC-day calls.n, source attempts and distinct-source count and increment calls.unsent, appending one reason event. No retroactive changes to historical counted calls. Compiler proposer refunds only its own reservation; paid cached cards remain spent.
implementation.worker: When L2 is enabled claim one at a time (excluding already visited jobs), stop after the first unsent adapter failure in either phase even following a successful call; defer the affected job with extraction_unavailable and return its queue attempt. Remaining records are unclaimed; next run_pending resets the tick hold and recovers.
implementation.read_only_reporting: ExtractionLedger.summary().calls and calls_today() are counted spend; summary().unsent_calls is separate. Owner discovery_summary forwards unsent_calls into existing BFF discovery_summary.llm_calls, and discovery-pipeline hypothesis_cards reports unsent_calls_today independently. Legacy readers without the column report unknown (None), not invented zero.

regression_proof: Actual socket connection refusal and resolver failure through the real HTTP client refund spend; ConnectionRefusedError raised after request() and an actual partial streaming response timeout remain counted.

Real client HTTP -> local HTTP bridge -> real FastAPI adapter structured route -> upstream boundary: policy RPC failure and policy deadline exhaustion never invoke provider and refund; provider 503, provider 504 and a provider message containing the policy marker remain counted.

Adapter-down tick with 10 queued records claims 1 and records 1 deferral; no queue or ledger attempt is spent. Also tested success followed by outage in the same tick. Healthy next tick processes every remaining record.
Compiler proposer policy failure refunds its reservation while retaining an earlier paid card call.

24 real parallel HTTP clients refund without losing another source spend; original-day refund survives UTC midnight; migration preserves historical n; 10,080 unsent-event cap preserves other outcome history.
Owner read and discovery probe report counted/unsent separately; each checked-in unsent reason has boundary coverage; typed result round-trip preserves the reason.

runtime_budget.cadence: Existing 60-second distillation tick; first unsent adapter failure stops it, <=1 outage attempt/event per tick (~1440/day). Input-budget refusals can additionally emit one event per processed record within the configured existing batch limit.
runtime_budget.counter: One new integer column calls.unsent in each existing daily calls row; no new daily rows, database file, table or recurring job; <=8 bytes extra per existing row.
runtime_budget.events: Use existing events with a partial unsent-only index. Source <=256 and detail <=500 characters: ~0.8 KB typical / <=3.2 KB UTF-8 payload per event, ~1 MiB typical / <=4.6 MB payload/day for persistent outage.
runtime_budget.cap_and_cleanup: At most 10080 unsent events (~8 MB typical / <=33 MB UTF-8 payload plus existing SQLite overhead), oldest pruned atomically on each unsent write. Partial index <=10080 keys; SQLite reuses freed pages. Original non-unsent history remains under RC3 WP3.1.

hosted_acceptance.authority: Next normal Root deployment/switch, after independent review and supervisor merge; read-only observations only, no induced outage or ledger rewrite.
procedure: Verify hosted manifest and every expected steady service at the deployed exact version; record the real release_switched_at, not process start or an inferred cutoff.

Around that next normal switch collect existing adapter/controller logs and read the existing ledger read-only. Correlate DNS/refused/policy failure events by timestamp; each must have outcome=unsent and a typed reason; no new corresponding counted unavailable failure is expected for a proven pre-model refusal.

Read SELECT day,n,unsent,cap,sources FROM calls WHERE day=date('now'); compare before/after observations for this switch; confirmed unsent failures increase unsent only, n stays <=cap (default 400). Historical already-spent cap is not reset by deployment.

Read recent existing events using id range and outcome=unsent, and the single affected queue row: extraction_unavailable with unchanged attempts; unaffected pending rows remain unclaimed. Next normal tick after adapter recovers resumes work.

Run the existing read-only discovery pipeline acceptance with configured ACCEPTANCE_BFF_URL / viewer credentials: python3 -m acceptance.discovery_pipeline_day; retain JSON showing hypothesis_cards.values.calls_today and unsent_calls_today separately. Other stage failures do not prove this accounting change failed or passed.
